note: Shared list locking the risky-pattern heuristic across runtimes. `risky` are patterns QRID_riskyPattern / CheckCharacter::riskyPattern must reject (config error, no compile); `safe` must pass through. The gate has two stages. Stage one rejects nested quantifiers (bounded and unbounded) AND any repetition of a group that can match ambiguously — alternation, optionals, or inner quantifiers — with inner groups collapsed layer by layer so nesting cannot hide the shape. Stage two-a rejects the POLYNOMIAL class stage one misses: two or more UNBOUNDED quantifiers (*, +, {n,}) over overlapping character classes with no mandatory separator between them (.*.*, [0-9]*[0-9]*, [A-Z]+[A-Z0-9]+). Stage two-b (F1) rejects a contiguous run of overlapping BOUNDED quantifiers whose product of per-factor match-length choices exceeds MAX_BACKTRACK_PRODUCT (1e6) — e.g. A{1,20}A{1,20}A{1,20}A{1,20}A{1,20} (=3.2M): each factor is bounded but the factor count is the backtracking exponent, so a long chain freezes a browser's engine even though PCRE2 auto-possessifies it, and unlike the server the client has no match-time backstop. Stage two-c (VAL-4) follows a chain of unbounded quantifiers over overlapping classes, joined by atoms that may match nothing or that the quantifier before them also matches (in .*-.*-.*X each "-" is also a "."); three or more in one chain are refused, two (.*x.*) pass. Before any stage, each escape is read as an atom of the same reach: \d \w \s as their ASCII classes, \D \W \S and an escaped metacharacter as any character, so [\w.]+_ keeps its "_" and [0-9]+\.[0-9]+ keeps its separator.It deliberately over-rejects (a repeated alternation is refused even with disjoint branches; a collapsed group is treated as overlapping everything). Still a heuristic, not a proof: a SHORT bounded backtracker under the budget like A{1,40}A{1,40}A{1,40}9 (=64000) passes, which is why the server keeps the match-time PCRE-error guard as a backstop. `risky_js.cjs` additionally times every `safe` pattern against adversarial input, so "safe" is measured, not assumed.
dialect_note: Patterns the two regex dialects read differently. `dialect_reject` must be refused by BOTH QRID_gatePattern (js) and CheckCharacter::gatePattern (php) - for any stated reason, but by both, because a pattern one runtime admits and the other refuses splits enforcement: either the browser stops checking the field while the post-save audit keeps filing findings, or the two engines both compile it and then disagree about every value. `dialect_accept` must be admitted by both. Round 3, M-1 and M-2. "{,n}" is literal to JavaScript and to PCRE2 before 10.43 but {0,n} from 10.43 (PHP 8.4), so it is refused too. VAL-5 adds verbs, \k'name', \k{name}, \o{...}, \8, \9 and class ranges at a shorthand escape; VAL-11 admits named groups.
